meta.purpose: P7833 South Mississippi Project after the October 28, 2026 binding open season: length 215 mi, diameter 42 in (or 36), Richland Parish LA to George County MS, start March 2030, status ref added

verifications.note: A Pipeline & Gas Journal news story from late October 2026. It says Energy Transfer Interstate Holdings launched a binding open season for the South Mississippi Project on October 28, 2026, closing November 25. The pipeline would run about 215 miles from a proposed receipt point in Richland Parish, Louisiana, to a new delivery point in the George County, Mississippi, area. It would be either 42-inch or 36-inch pipe. The company has binding commitments from anchor shippers, plans to seek FERC approval, and expects service on or before March 1, 2030.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Status stays proposed. Energy Transfer opened a binding open season on October 28, 2026, and says it has binding commitments from anchor shippers. It has not yet decided to build and has not filed with FERC. The Pipeline & Gas Journal story is added beside the existing refs.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Changed from 150 miles to 215 miles. The binding open season of October 2026 describes about 215 miles of new pipe from Richland Parish, Louisiana, to George County, Mississippi. The 150 miles came from the EIA August 2026 workbook, which lists 100 to 150 miles from the 2024 non-binding open season. That figure is older than the redesign, so its ref is replaced.

The 2024 non-binding open season named receipt points around Carthage, Texas, and EIA still lists Texas as the start.
